findings.title: RESIDUAL Android unit-test source set references AiTask/AiProviderRouter.candidates() whi
evidence: [E:app/src/test/java/com/example/AiProviderRouterTest.kt:L4-L27]
[E:cmd#22 git grep -n 'fun candidates' -- '*.kt' -> no output, exit 1]
[E:cmd#22 git grep -n AiTask -- '*.kt' -> only AiProviderRouterTest.kt lines 4,12,19,26]
[E:app/src/main/java/com/example/data/remote/AiProviderRouter.kt:L16-L44 single diagnose() method, no candidates(), no AiTask enum]
[E:.github/workflows/ZWNJ-apkbuild.yml:L20-L26 step 'Force Build APK (Ignore AI Errors)' runs gradlew assembleDebug -x lint -x test]
findings.impact: The stale AiTask/candidates() references are gone (grep returns 0 for both) and the replacement test only touches symbols that exist in app/src/main. The Gradle compile itself was NOT executed - no JDK or Android SDK in this sandbox - so the compile-clean claim is unproven. || original impact: The declared test task cannot compile, so README's gradlew testDebugUnitTest, the build.yml 'Run unit tests' step and therefore every Android release proof fail. A bypass workflow that skips tests exists, which is how APKs are still produced.
findings.exploit_or_repro: gradlew testDebugUnitTest (NOT executed here: no JDK/Android SDK) -> unresolved reference AiTask. Static proof is complete: AiTask is imported from com.example.data.remote, the app's own namespace, and no declaration exists in the module.
findings.remediation: Rewrite AiProviderRouterTest against the real AiProviderRouter contract (server gateway URL, bearer header, images.take(2), error mapping) or delete the stale tests.

findings.title: RESIDUAL No server read API exists for orders, quotes, devices or passport history
evidence: [E:cmd#20 harness J3.1 -> GET /v1/devices 404; GET /v1/orders 404]
[E:cmd#12 route inventory: the only GET routes are /health, /v1/public/features, /v1/me]
[E:README.md device-passport section claims the history is written from server-side order state and survives reinstall]
findings.impact: Order history is now server-backed and executed (GET /v1/orders, GET /v1/orders/:orderId, IDOR probe 404). DeviceEntity itself still has no server API, so the passport's device record remains Room-local. || original impact: The device passport and order history are Room-local only. The README's central durability promise is unmet: reinstalling the app or changing phone erases the record. Support, warranty claims and disputes have nothing server-side to read.
findings.exploit_or_repro: GET /v1/orders with a valid bearer token -> 404 (executed).
findings.remediation: Add GET /v1/orders and GET /v1/orders/:orderId (quotes, acceptance, evidence, escrow hold), scoped strictly to claims.sub or the approved technician/operator.

findings.title: No CI job builds or tests the server that owns OTP, payments and the ledger
evidence: [E:cmd#14 .github/workflows/build.yml:L1-L36 only JDK, Android SDK, gradlew test, assembleDebug]
[E:cmd#14 .github/workflows/android-apk.yml:L1-L60 gradle only]
[E:cmd#22 grep -rn npm .github/workflows -> no match]
findings.impact: The 18 passing server tests run only on a developer laptop. A regression in the money path can merge to main with no automated gate.
findings.remediation: Add .github/workflows/server.yml: checkout, setup-node 22, npm ci, npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high, npm test inside services/auth-api.

findings.title: Every workflow run in repository history has failed; the latest main run died at Set up Android SDK
evidence: [E:cmd#15 gh run list --repo reARbitRA/Tamirkar --limit 10 -> 10 rows, all failure, newest 36493298453 on main]
[E:cmd#16 gh run view 36493298453 -> X build in 11s with X Set up Android SDK and all later steps skipped]
findings.impact: There is no green build in this repository's history. The README claim that CI provisions exactly that toolchain is contradicted by observed runs.
findings.remediation: Pin android-actions/setup-android to a maintained version, install the SDK explicitly, and split the server job so the money path has a green gate independent of Android toolchain churn.

findings.title: Workflow triggers are pinned to stale branch names, so PRs run no CI at all
evidence: [E:.github/workflows/build.yml:L4-L6 branches main, master, arena/01a03dca-tamirkar]
[E:.github/workflows/android-apk.yml:L4-L7 branches arena/01a03c31-tamirkar only]
[E:cmd#14 no pull_request trigger in any workflow]
findings.impact: A pull request can merge with zero checks. android-apk.yml can only ever run on one dead branch.
findings.remediation: Trigger on push to main plus pull_request; repoint the dead branch filters.

findings.title: RESIDUAL No backup, restore, RPO/RTO or point-in-time-recovery procedure exists anywhere
evidence: [E:cmd#27 git ls-files | grep -iE backup|restore|pg_dump -> only app/src/main/res/xml/backup_rules.xml (Android auto-backup rules)]
[E:cmd#27 git grep -i backup|pg_dump|restore over yml/yaml/sh/js -> no server match]
[E:LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md T-1 day requires backups completed and an isolated restore test meeting documented RPO/RTO]
findings.impact: backup/restore scripts written and their tool preflight and populated-DB refusal executed (exit 4 with a clear message). No real pg_dump/pg_restore round-trip: postgresql-client is absent from this sandbox. RPO/RTO documented but the drill is not done. || original impact: The database holds phone numbers, KYC document references, payment intents and an append-only ledger. A lost volume is unrecoverable and the ledger cannot be reconstructed.
findings.remediation: Script pg_dump/pg_restore on a schedule, record RPO/RTO, add a restore-drill step to the runbook. Managed Postgres with PITR is the cheaper path for a Render pilot.

findings.title: All legal documents are unapproved internal drafts; the approvals matrix is 0/6
evidence: [E:docs/legal/TERMS_FA.md:L3 status banner: internal draft, no legal approval]
[E:docs/legal/PRIVACY_FA.md:L3 same draft banner]
[E:docs/legal/APPROVALS.md:L5-L10 six unchecked boxes including counsel sign-off on privacy, terms, cancellation/refund and warranty]
findings.impact: Collecting payment and holding 15% of it in escrow without counsel-approved terms, a dated privacy notice or a registered legal entity is a legal prohibition on public launch.
findings.remediation: Counsel review and dated publication of all five documents; fill APPROVALS.md with names and dates. Requires a human lawyer - cannot be automated.

findings.title: POST /v1/ai/diagnoses has no per-user or per-IP rate limit - unbounded provider spend
evidence: [E:services/auth-api/src/server.js:L274-L294 no limiter before generateDiagnosis]
[E:services/auth-api/src/ai.js:L60-L75 one Gemini generateContent call per request, 20 s timeout]
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can loop this endpoint and drive real Gemini spend and quota exhaustion; the OTP path is rate-limited but the paid AI path is not.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Static read; not load-tested in this sandbox.
findings.remediation: Add a per-user sliding-window limit (e.g. 10/hour) plus a global concurrency cap around the provider call.

findings.title: POST /v1/technicians/apply self-elevates any customer to role=technician and re-issues the token
evidence: [E:services/auth-api/src/server.js:L296-L323 UPDATE users SET role=technician then issueSession with role technician]
[E:cmd#20 harness J7.1 -> 202 with new_token_role=technician]
findings.impact: Role escalation with no human gate. Downstream money actions are still blocked by requireApprovedTechnician(), so impact is limited to technician-only surfaces and to blurring the customer/technician separation the KYC flow depends on.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Executed: customer token in, technician token out, verification_status still unsubmitted.
findings.remediation: Keep the applicant at role=customer until an operator approves KYC; grant the technician role inside the approval transaction.

findings.title: No retry or backoff on any outbound provider call
evidence: [E:services/auth-api/src/kavenegar.js:L8-L19 single fetch, 10 s timeout, no retry]
[E:services/auth-api/src/zarinpal.js:L8-L19 single fetch, 15 s timeout, no retry]
[E:services/auth-api/src/ai.js:L60-L75 single fetch, 20 s timeout, no retry]
findings.impact: One transient provider blip becomes a user-visible 502. In Iran, where cross-border egress is unstable, that will be the common case rather than the exception.
findings.remediation: Add bounded exponential backoff with jitter (2-3 attempts) for idempotent calls, plus a circuit breaker on repeated failure.

findings.title: Duplicate orphan CI files and a zero-width-named workflow that builds with tests disabled
evidence: [E:cmd#11 git ls-files lists ci/android-apk.yml and github/workflows/build.yml (github/, not .github/)]
[E:cmd#27 diff shows both differ from their .github/workflows counterparts - stale copies, not includes]
[E:.github/workflows/ apkbuild.yml filename begins with U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER]
[E:.github/workflows/ apkbuild.yml:L20-L26 step Force Build APK (Ignore AI Errors) runs gradlew assembleDebug -x lint -x test]
findings.impact: Three near-identical workflow definitions with no single source of truth, plus a workflow whose explicit purpose is to ship an APK with lint and tests skipped. That is the mechanism by which F-EXEC-001 stayed invisible.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Executed diffs and filename byte inspection.
findings.remediation: Delete the ci/ and github/ duplicates, consolidate to one workflow per target, and retire the test-skipping workflow once F-EXEC-001 is fixed.

findings.title: RESIDUAL Dockerfile uses a floating base tag, has no HEALTHCHECK and does not set NODE_EN
evidence: [E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L1 FROM node:22-alpine with no digest pin]
[E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L1-L10 (10 lines total) no HEALTHCHECK instruction and no ENV NODE_ENV]
[E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L9 USER node - non-root, correct]
findings.impact: ENV NODE_ENV=production and a HEALTHCHECK against /health added. The base image is still a floating tag: pinning it needs a registry lookup and hub.docker.com / registry-1.docker.io both fail TLS here. Left as a documented open item rather than inventing a digest. || original impact: Rebuilds are not reproducible: the same commit can produce different images. Without HEALTHCHECK an orchestrator can route traffic to a container whose migrations failed.
findings.remediation: Pin by digest, add ENV NODE_ENV=production and a HEALTHCHECK against /health.

findings.title: Zarinpal callback is an unauthenticated public GET with no shared secret
evidence: [E:services/auth-api/src/server.js:L587-L638 no auth; authority regex then verifyZarinpalPayment]
[E:services/auth-api/src/zarinpal.js:L40-L51 verification re-checks merchant_id, amount and authority against verify.json]
findings.impact: Correctness rests entirely on the provider round-trip, which is the right design for Zarinpal, but there is no second factor. Anyone who learns an authority can trigger verification attempts and enumerate callback outcomes.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Static read; the ledger is additionally protected by the status != paid guard and the idempotency key.
findings.remediation: Bind the callback to the intent by embedding the intent id in the callback URL path and requiring it to match the authority's intent.

findings.title: Migrations are forward-only with no down path or tested repair procedure
evidence: [E:services/auth-api/src/migrate.js:L1-L37 applies numbered files forward and records them in schema_migrations; no reverse]
[E:LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md rollback step 6 says roll back only the artifact until migrations have a tested down/forward repair procedure]
findings.impact: A bad migration in production has no rehearsed undo. The team acknowledged this in its own checklist but has not closed it.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Static read; migrate.js executed successfully in-session (exit 0, three migrations applied).
findings.remediation: Adopt a down-migration convention or document and rehearse a snapshot-restore procedure before enabling payments.

findings.title: server.js is a 694-line god file holding all 16 routes, validation and money logic
evidence: [E:cmd#8 wc -l -> 694 services/auth-api/src/server.js; next largest source file is 490]
findings.impact: Every change to auth, AI, KYC, orders, payments and escrow touches one file, raising merge-conflict and regression risk exactly where the money lives.
findings.remediation: Extract route groups into modules sharing one app factory; keep the ledger and state machine in domain modules.

findings.title: Room MIGRATION_1_2 is a no-op that exists only to absorb a version bump
evidence: [E:app/src/main/java/com/example/data/local/TamirkarDatabase.kt:L66-L72 override fun migrate(db) = Unit]
findings.impact: Harmless today and correctly non-destructive, but it teaches the pattern of bumping schema versions without migration content.
findings.remediation: Either revert version to 1 or document why the bump happened; enable exportSchema and check schemas in.

findings.title: Android toolchain absent in the audit sandbox - client build and test are UNTESTABLE here
evidence: [E:cmd#5 java --version -> NOT FOUND; javac NOT FOUND; gradle NOT FOUND]
[E:cmd#5 ANDROID_HOME=unset, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT=unset, no ~/Android]

findings.title: Zarinpal sandbox unreachable from the audit sandbox - payment capture and the 85/15 split are UNTESTABLE
evidence: [E:cmd#20 harness J5.1 -> POST /v1/payments/zarinpal/start returned 502 payment_unavailable]
[E:cmd#20 harness J5.2 -> payment_intents row created then marked status=failed with amount_tomans 800000 / amount_rials 8000000]
[E:cmd#17 curl repo1.maven.org -> SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL; sandbox egress is restricted to the npm registry and the GitHub API]
findings.impact: The most money-critical path (callback -> verify -> ledger split -> escrow hold) has no executed evidence in this audit. The failure path IS proven correct: intent created, provider failure recorded, user gets a Persian 502.
findings.remediation: Run the capture path in CI against the Zarinpal sandbox with a real merchant id, or add a provider-port seam so the callback logic can be integration-tested offline.

findings.title: No data-deletion capability; the privacy and security mailboxes are unproven
evidence: [E:docs/legal/PRIVACY_FA.md:L9 users may request deletion via privacy@oosta.app]
[E:SECURITY.md:L8 states if that mailbox has not been configured yet, contact the repository owner privately]
[E:cmd#12 route inventory: no DELETE route exists on any resource]
findings.impact: The privacy notice promises a deletion right the API cannot honour. Under GDPR/CCPA-equivalent regimes that is a compliance gap, and the named mailbox is admitted to possibly not exist.
findings.remediation: Add an operator-only account-deletion/redaction path and confirm both mailboxes resolve before publishing the notice.
